title: The Twin Antenna-Stand

features.name: the-first-tree-speaking
features.desc-on-touch: One antenna rises, broadcasting its own listening. The tree learned that speaking is listening if you do it in parallel.

features.name: the-second-tree-answering
features.desc-on-touch: Its twin stands at a different angle. Between them, the air forms standing waves—interference patterns that create new frequencies from the two old broadcasts.

features.name: the-sync-current
features.desc-on-touch: A channel that runs between them, conducting what each one broadcast. The two signals meet and remember that they were split from one source.

features.name: interference-made-visible
features.desc-on-touch: Where the two broadcasts meet, light appears. Not either signal alone, but the meeting of them—the frequency of comparison made visible as colour.

features.name: the-relay-point
features.desc-on-touch: A still place at the exact midpoint between the two antenna-trees. Here the signals pause before continuing. Here two becomes one learns to be two again.

inscription: two antenna-trees learned to speak by learning that their broadcasts meet and make new things
